Subject: AWS Marketplace usage licensing & fulfillment playbook

Hi Lindsey and team,

Thanks again for the call this morning — really helpful to walk through the private-offer + metering options for Acme Analytics. I wanted to capture a concrete, prioritized plan so we can move the engineering and legal checklists in parallel. High-level asks below; I added owners.

Quick context: Acme wants a Private Offer with usage-based billing (monthly invoice driven by AWS metering calls). They will buy via Seller Central and expect entitlement validation inside our app so seats/features unlock for their users.

Top-line playbook (proposal):
- Seller setup (Owner: Marissa)
  - Confirm Redwood seller account in Seller Central and product listing created (SaaS product).
  - Ensure product code and pricing dimensions align with our metering model (monthly usage + seat minimum).

- Entitlement & Fulfillment integration (Owner: Karthik)
  - Integrate AWS Entitlement API to validate subscriptions at login/on boarding; cache entitlement token server-side for performance.
  - Implement metering calls to AWS Metering API for incremental usage events (RegisterUsage or equivalent) and reconcile daily with AWS reports.

- Private Offer & Contract (Owner: Jonas + Legal)
  - Draft Private Offer terms (Doc attached: acme_private_offer_terms.docx) and route to Acme for signature (DocuSign link to follow).
  - Confirm invoicing expectations (AWS will bill Acme; Redwood will receive payout per Seller Central settlement).

- Test & Go-live (Owner: Rishi)
  - Create a test buyer account in Seller Central and walk through the subscription + entitlement flow (test instructions attached).
  - End-to-end smoke test: purchase, entitlement appears, usage metering recorded, settlement line appears in Seller Central transaction report.

Open questions we flagged on the call that need AWS confirmation:
1) Exact metering API names & idempotency guarantees for our expected bursty telemetry.
2) Recommended reconciliation cadence and sample reports we should consume from Seller Central.
3) Guidance on private-offer billing lag (when entitlement becomes active after purchase).

Can you confirm AWS can support the above and point us at any existing Redwood/AWS reference code or docs? If you prefer, we can book a follow-up tech call next week to go through the API steps line-by-line.

Attachments: redwood_aws_playbook_draft.pdf, acme_private_offer_terms.docx

Thanks — Rishi

Hi Rishi — great summary, thanks for laying this out. Happy to confirm and add a few clarifications from the Marketplace side.

Quick answers to your open questions:
1) Metering API & idempotency: the SaaS metering flow uses the RegisterUsage (metering) API. It accepts a UsageRecord with timestamp and quantity; calls should be idempotent if you set a unique UsageRecordId for each logical event. For bursty events, batch locally and call RegisterUsage for aggregated windows (we recommend 5–15s windows for high-throughput).

2) Reconciliation reports: Seller Central provides daily settlement reports and a Usage Records report. You can pull CSVs from the Reports tab or subscribe to S3 export; many sellers reconcile nightly against their own aggregated counters.

3) Private Offer activation window: Private Offers become active once AWS processes the contract and the buyer accepts. In practice this can be minutes to hours depending on DocuSign flow and AWS processing. We recommend a short retry/backoff entitlement-check on purchase confirmation (poll for up to 30 minutes) with a customer-facing status of "Provisioning".

Implementation notes / resources:
- Entitlement API: call AWS Entitlement service in your onboarding flow to verify buyer subscription and SKU entitlements. Cache for 1 hour unless you expect real-time changes.
- Metering best practice: aggregate events server-side to reduce API calls and use unique ids for idempotency.
- Seller Central test buy: use the Test Buy flow in Seller Central to simulate purchases; follow the Seller Central doc for creating a test buyer account (link: https://aws.amazon.com/marketplace/test-buy).

I'll loop in Seller Support for any deep API questions; they can share sample code snippets. If you want, I can also schedule a 60-minute integration call with our Partner Solutions Architect next Tuesday.

Cc'd: aws-marketplace-saas@amazon.com for sample code access.

Best,
Lindsey

Thanks everyone — good progress. Quick ownership updates and next actions from Legal/Finance: 

1) Legal (Jonas) — I reviewed the attached Acme PO terms. Narrow set of edits requested: clarify liability cap tied to fees paid via AWS for 12 months, and add a short clause about data retention (we will not store raw customer analytics logs longer than 90 days). Sending redline via DocuSign shortly.

2) Finance (Jonas) — I pinged Accounting for settlement cadence and they confirmed: AWS posts settlements approximately 14–21 days after the monthly usage billing period, with the possibility of holdbacks for refunds/disputes. I'll get a finance note into the HubSpot deal record.

3) Engineering (Karthik) — please target a small spike this week to wire up entitlement checks and a test RegisterUsage call. Use the test buy flow Marissa created; I'll coordinate with Acme billing contact on the timing (cc'd).

- Jonas: upload redlined contract to DocuSign and share link (by EOD 3/19).
